title: Immunofluorescent staining of cancer spheroids and fine-needle aspiration-derived organoids
protocol: Fix the organoids.
Aspirate media from the wells of disc culture, leaving only the Matrigel discs containing the spheroids/organoids.
Put 2 mL of fixative in each well and incubate plate at 4°C for 15 min.
Swirl the plate by hand and place back at 4°C for another 15 min.
Pipette to break up the Matrigel and transfer into a labeled 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Resuspend pellets in 1 mL Antibody Dilution Buffer.
Place on rotator for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to block.
For fibroblast/tumor cell staining: Add both the anti-smooth muscle actin antibody and the anti-cytokeratin 8/18 antibody at a dilution of 1:250 directly to the Antibody Dilution Buffer.
For β-catenin staining: Add the anti-β-catenin antibody to a final dilution of 1:500 directly to the Antibody Dilution Buffer.
Place on rotator at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Add anti-guinea pig and anti-rabbit secondary antibodies, each at a dilution of 1:250, directly to the Antibody Dilution Buffer/organoid suspension.
Place on rotator in the dark at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 3 hours.
Wash organoids in Antibody Dilution Buffer.
Resuspend pellet in 0.1% TBSTX.
Add Hoechst at a 1:1000 dilution directly to 0.1% TBSTX, rotate for 20 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C) in the dark.
Repeat wash step in Antibody Dilution Buffer.
Resuspend pellet in 0.1% TBSTX.
Add phalloidin at a 1:100 dilution directly to 0.1% TBSTX, rotate for 20 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C) in the dark.
Repeat wash step in Antibody Dilution Buffer.
Remove as much of the supernatant as possible without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend organoids in 50 μL PBS with a P200 with the end of the tip cut off.
Pipette the organoid suspension onto a labeled slide.
Allow the organoids to settle.
Tip the slide slightly so that the PBS pools in one spot.
Aspirate the PBS carefully without disturbing the organoids.
Pipette 50 μL Prolong Gold Antifade onto the slide.
Place a coverslip over the slide without creating bubbles.
Seal the edges with clear nail polish and allow to cure in the dark for 5–10 minutes.
Store in a dark box at 4°C until ready to image.
On the microscope, use the focusing adjustment knobs to adjust the z-plane down to the bottom of the organoid of interest and select it as “bottom.”
Adjust the z-plane up to the top of the organoid and select it as “top.”
Use the recommended step size (typically 1–2 um).
Select “create Z-stack.”
Save the file.
Image from the longest wavelength to the shortest wavelength to prevent bleaching.
Start with low magnifications before going to higher magnifications.
Perform analysis of your choice.
